title: PR body's fold-only proof pairs the pre-5.11 hash with the intermediate-fold tick-1; the literal pair FAILS fold-check
evidence: pr-bodies/5.11.md:50: "- **Fold chain:** `66c4324a06058860` (pre-5.11) → `250679b1940fb87b` (5.11 data) → `17d3baf8c6e1df7f` (comment-accuracy fold, same PR)." :51: "with the previous hash spliced at the fold position (bytes 33..40), FNV-hashes to the previous golden tick-1 **exactly** (`ab1fb0d04a90026c`)". Verified at the reviewed head: `./bin/foldcheck_harness fold-check 66c4324a06058860 ab1fb0d04a90026c` → "spliced prev      6c24e9cec592aece" → "FAIL"; `git show 11c6cf6~1:goldens/boot.t1` shows "catalog_hash 66c4324a06058860 ... 1 6c24e9cec592aece" while `git show d0c2c38~1:goldens/boot.t1` shows "catalog_hash 250679b1940fb87b ... 1 ab1fb0d04a90026c" (both pairings verified PASS: fold-check 250679b1940fb87b ab1fb0d04a90026c → exit 0).
detail: The cited tick-1 belongs to the intermediate catalog 250679b1940fb87b, but the body never names which hash is spliced; a verifier pairing the chain's pre-5.11 hash with the cited tick-1 gets a false FAIL.
recommended_fix: Name the spliced hash next to the value: "with `250679b1940fb87b` spliced … hashes to `ab1fb0d04a90026c`" (or cite the 66c4324a06058860/6c24e9cec592aece pair).

title: usage() output omits the new fold-check verb
evidence: harness/main.odin:275: `fmt.eprintln("usage: harness run|save [demo...] [--stats-out <path>] | replay <demo> <log.bin> | drift-check | preview-check | stats-check <demo> | input-parity [save] | palcheck | map-preview <seed> [out.png]")` — no fold-check. Verified live: `./bin/foldcheck_harness fold-check` (wrong arity) prints this line without the verb, then exits 2.
detail: The diff added the fold-check verb (main.odin:143-149) and its header comment, but the canonical usage line — the only discoverability surface on a bad invocation — omits it.
recommended_fix: Add `| fold-check <prev-hash> <prev-tick1>` to the usage() string in harness/main.odin:275.

title: Unused `import "core:os"` in harness/fold_check.odin
evidence: harness/fold_check.odin:19: `import "core:os"`; `grep -c "os\." harness/fold_check.odin` → `0` (the file's body uses only fmt/strconv/pp + builtins; os.exit lives in main.odin, not here).
detail: Dead import in the new file — os is never referenced in fold_check.odin; nothing else needs it.
